title: The rtists package, inside and out
text: rtists wraps fiber tractography objects (streamline, bundle, bundle_set) interactive 3-D visualisations. whole package one sentence: fiber object flows internal long-data-frame pipeline one two htmlwidget backends, three.js renderer (default) plotly scatter3d plot. dependency shape deliberately light: compiled code SystemRequirements, central package’s CRAN-clean posture. 3-D rendering happens entirely browser via vendored JavaScript. exported API small: plot3d(): S7 generic methods three fiber classes. Returns htmlwidget. prune(): S7 generic thins overlapping bundle spread-subset whose tubes touch. fatten(): S7 generic attaches visible tube radius streamlines carry none. Everything else internal. fiber classes namespaced (fiber::streamline ), plain S3 dispatch breaks , rtists uses S7 generics methods declared S7 classes directly. per-class data-frame conversion helpers (.streamline_to_df, .bundle_to_df, .bundle_set_to_df) plain internal functions rather S3/S7 methods, precisely class names carry :: prefix S3 dispatch match.

title: The rtists package, inside and out
text: three.js backend lives R/backend-threejs.R, builds widget payload, inst/htmlwidgets/lib/threejs/rtists-render.js, renders . naive widget send coordinates JSON floating-point numbers (17 significant digits ). even 100k-point bundle bloats widget JSON enormously. rtists instead packs numerical buffers raw binary little-endian lets htmlwidgets base64-encode byte strings, giving compact payloads: JS side decodes back atob typed-array views (b64ToF32, b64ToU8F32). Positions radii cross wire Float32 precision; colours cross 8-bit channels, exactly canvas samples anyway. widget branches mode field set R side. line2 mode (default). single LineSegments2 mesh LineMaterial({ worldUnits: true, vertexColors: true, linewidth }). Interleaved segment buffers [start, end] per segment, per-segment start/end colours. everything one draw call, path scales large bundles default. Constant world-space width via linewidth uniform. classic three.js resolution footgun (unset resolution uniform producing NaN aspect shader) self-healed r186 LineSegmentsGeometry’s onBeforeRender hook, manual handling needed. tube mode. One TubeGeometry per streamline, built unit radius around CatmullRomCurve3, every ring vertices displaced radially streamline’s per-point radius, per-vertex color attribute supplies fill. tube built unit radius displaced, single geometry can represent radius varies along streamline. Object-level depth sorting gives transparent tubes: tube mesh transparent: true depthWrite: false, transparent tubes compose correctly instead flickering. rtists never decides radius beyond ask , never shrinks tubes hides streamlines dodge overlap. Overlap generator’s business, rtists’s. radius argument resolves small set helpers: .df_radius_from_data(df) recovers radius carried object : radius column resolved frame. radius constant within streamline returns per-streamline vector; otherwise per-point vector; NULL usable positive radius exists. NULL / 0: fast line2 (either “use object’s radius” “plain thin lines”). positive scalar: constant-radius tubes. per-streamline vector (length == number streamlines). per-point vector (length == total number points). widget ships small -scene DOM tooltip. pointer move raycasts mesh, maps hit back packed point index, renders pinned bundle name coordinates plus toggleable attribute columns. Line2 mode maps raycast segment index point via segToPoint index; tube mode finds nearest point within hit streamline. separate legend panel (.df_legend_meta) lets user remap aesthetics live without re-framing camera: colour bundle attribute, radius numeric attribute (tube mode), per-bundle per-streamline visibility. R side ships 3 x 256 Uint8 colour ramp plus per-streamline per-point attribute buffers; JS side rebuilds mesh place decoded buffers. Anything missing (NULL/NaN value) painted distinct grey, never dropped silently.

title: The rtists package, inside and out
text: plot3d() renders whatever given. bundles thin streamlines carry radius, picture can tangle overlapping lines. prune() fatten() companion utilities turn dense bundle legible one. prune(x, radius, overlap_margin = 1, max_iter = Inf) returns subset whose tubes given radius overlap. core .prune_indices(polys, radius, overlap_margin, max_iter): Required separation: req = 2 * radius * overlap_margin (tube diameter, scaled margin). Two streamlines count “overlapping” .min_sep_two (closest approach two polyline geometries) least req. nothing kept yet, consider remaining streamlines raw index order; otherwise, among remaining streamlines, choose farthest-first: one whose gap kept set (.streamline_cover_gap) largest, ties broken index, keep first one whose tube overlap kept tube (every .min_sep_two least req). Stop soon every remaining streamline “covered” (.streamline_cover_gap <= radius, meaning kept tubes already span whole hull given radius), remaining streamline non-overlapping candidate. result sort(keep): deterministic, reproducible spread. Beyond index tie-break outcome depend input order, bundle prunes way every time. fatten(x, visibility = NULL, ...) attaches constant per-streamline radius radius-less streamlines render tubes instead hairline lines. chooses radius geometry: .fatten_step(polys): median intra-streamline sampling step (median distance consecutive points along streamline). .fatten_dmin(polys): minimum distance two streamlines. .fatten_floor(polys, visibility): visible-radius floor. Either user-supplied visibility (validated single positive number), median step sensible default. bundle method decides two regimes streamlines sit relative one another, f floor dmin closest approach: Sparse (dmin / 2 >= f): streamlines far enough apart tubes radius dmin / 2 just touch. Everything kept, radius: visually fullest picture overlap. Dense (dmin / 2 < f): streamlines overlap visible radius, fatten() falls back pruning: radius r=fr = f (floor) kept .prune_indices(polys, f, 1) subset, giving non-overlapping tubes visible floor. bundle_set method simply applies fatten() bundle turn drops become empty. subtle important detail: fatten() attach radius nested streamline. calls fiber::bundle() hoists per-streamline metadata bundle-level @streamline_data slot (per-streamline vector length S), rather nesting inside streamline. slot plot3d() reads back via .df_radius_from_data(), fattened radius flows straight pipeline. bundle fatten() returns renders tubes bare plot3d(x) call radius argument: radius now lives object’s data. fatten() method single streamline always applies visibility floor (nothing prune), empty-bundle case handled explicitly fiber::bundle(list()).
code: fiber::bundle(kept, streamline_data = list(radius = rep(r, length(kept))))

what: Assessment: three.js vs rgl vs plotly vs Rust
title: The rtists package, inside and out
text: comparison motivated three.js choice, question whether keep plotly backend one day move renderer native code. Strengths. single LineSegments2 draw call plus per-vertex colour buffers scales large bundles. Real world-space tube geometry (TubeGeometry + radial displacement) gives genuine 3-D thickness Phong flat shading, rgl gives plotly . Object-level depth-sorted transparency renders overlapping transparent tubes correctly. stays self-contained inline htmlwidget SystemRequirements compiled code, preserving CRAN-clean posture. Costs. plotting code JavaScript. Engineering (payload encoding, ESM loading trick, two render paths, hover + legend) one-time effort hundred lines JS. --shelf rthreejs package thin wrapper suited level control, rtists vendors three.js directly. rgl offers true OpenGL lighting interactive rglwidget(), usual tool tractography. adopting mean: adding SystemRequirements (GLEW/GLU/GL Linux, X systems), broke “SystemRequirements” CRAN posture motivated design; lines3d() issues one GL draw call per line, slow huge bundles compared single LineSegments draw call; continuous per-point colour single line requires splitting per segment sub-lines vary colour; widget still opens GL context needs virtual framebuffer headless CI. three.js renderer can approach rgl’s “cinematic” look (tubes, lighting, depth-sorted transparency) without costs. two backends assessed r186 upgrade. plotly renders flat, screen-space line strips: real thickness, lighting, depth-sorted transparency. r186 credible payoff (line width, interactivity) upgrade removed, original justification gone. rtists keeps two specific reasons: backend honours ..., forwarding plotly::layout() (handy titles scene tweaks); resilient second renderer WebGL unavailable. therefore exposed backend = "plotly", explicit opt-rather default. binding constraint large bundles renderer. Per whole-brain benchmark (5 M points), htmlwidget backends limited JSON text encoding payload: roughly 278 MB binary floats become around 444 MB JSON gigabyte HTML, taking 4-52 s just serialise. 10^5 points everything instant; 10^6 10^7 points saved inline widget becomes impractical either backend, htmlwidgets sharing serialisation ceiling. escape Rust implementation offer local server architecture: transfer binary floats WebSocket (WASM), avoiding JSON text entirely. rtists deliberately static, self-contained htmlwidget: embeddable, shareable, openable saved .html. streaming server invert contract (widget becomes client running local process) add compiled server dependency, exactly package avoids. reassessment concluded WebSocket/streaming backend: pay scale beyond htmlwidget’s practical range regardless transport, sacrifices self-contained artifact. whole-brain self-contained output ever truly needed 10^6+ points, path genuinely binary-embedded artifact (base64 blob Float32Array fetched within one HTML file), server rtists must ship. overwhelming majority tractography work (single tracts whole bundles, tens hundreds thousands points), three.js htmlwidget right shape: native dependencies, real 3-D tubes transparency, fast single-draw-call default. plotly backend stays opt-, ...-honouring fallback. Rust local-server rewrite justified 10^6-point scale ceiling, even fights htmlwidget’s core promise self-contained, shareable artifact.

what: rgl (the neuroimaging standard) – why it loses
title: The rtists package, inside and out
text: rgl offers true OpenGL lighting interactive rglwidget(), usual tool tractography. adopting mean: adding SystemRequirements (GLEW/GLU/GL Linux, X systems), broke “SystemRequirements” CRAN posture motivated design; lines3d() issues one GL draw call per line, slow huge bundles compared single LineSegments draw call; continuous per-point colour single line requires splitting per segment sub-lines vary colour; widget still opens GL context needs virtual framebuffer headless CI. three.js renderer can approach rgl’s “cinematic” look (tubes, lighting, depth-sorted transparency) without costs.

title: Getting started with rtists
text: streamline stores three compartments, accessible @ operator: @points — n×3n \times 3 numeric matrix columns X, Y, Z. @point_data — named list per-point numeric vectors (length nn), e.g. fractional anisotropy (FA) sampled along tract. @streamline_data — named list numeric scalars (length 1), e.g. tract-level mean FA. bundle holds: @streamlines — list streamline objects. @bundle_data — named list bundle-level metadata. bundle just list streamlines wrapped bundle():
code: pts <- matrix(   c(     0, 0, 0,     1, 2, 1,     2, 3, 3,     3, 3, 5,     4, 2, 6,     5, 1, 7   ),   ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE,   dimnames = list(NULL, c("X", "Y", "Z")) )  sl <- streamline(   points          = pts,   point_data      = list(FA = c(0.25, 0.40, 0.65, 0.70, 0.55, 0.30)),   streamline_data = list(mean_FA = 0.475) )  sl #>  #> ── Object of class `fiber::streamline()` with 6 points. ── #>  #> • Point attributes: "FA" #> • Streamline attributes: "mean_FA" #> # Simulate a small bundle of four slightly perturbed copies set.seed(42) streamlines <- lapply(seq_len(4), function(i) {   noise <- matrix(rnorm(nrow(pts) * 3, sd = 0.15), ncol = 3)   colnames(noise) <- c("X", "Y", "Z")   streamline(     points          = pts + noise,     point_data      = list(FA = pmin(pmax(sl@point_data$FA + rnorm(6, sd = 0.05), 0), 1)),     streamline_data = list(mean_FA = mean(sl@point_data$FA))   ) })  bun <- bundle(streamlines) bun #>  #> ── Object of class `fiber::bundle()` with 4 streamliness and [6–6] points per streamline. ── #>  #> • Point attributes: "FA" #> • Streamline attributes: "mean_FA" #> • Bundle attributes: none #>

what: Tissue Integrity Superimposed on Tractography Streamlines
title: Tissue Integrity Superimposed on Tractography Streamlines
text: rtists (R Tissue Integrity Superimposed Tractography Streamlines) provides interactive 3-D visualisation tractography streamlines bundles defined fiber package. main function plot3d(), S7 generic methods fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, fiber::bundle_set objects. default backend = "threejs" uses self-contained three.js widget real world-space line thickness (thickness) depth-sorted transparency; backend = "plotly" retained interim fallback. fully interactive (pan, rotate, zoom). static figures exported plotly backend.

title: Tissue Integrity Superimposed on Tractography Streamlines
text: Install latest CRAN release: current development version GitHub:
code: install.packages("rtists") # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("tractoverse/rtists")

title: Tissue Integrity Superimposed on Tractography Streamlines
code: library(rtists) library(fiber)  pts <- matrix(   c(     0, 0, 0,     1, 2, 1,     2, 3, 3,     3, 3, 5,     4, 2, 6,     5, 1, 7   ),   ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE,   dimnames = list(NULL, c("X", "Y", "Z")) )  sl <- streamline(   points          = pts,   point_data      = list(FA = c(0.25, 0.40, 0.65, 0.70, 0.55, 0.30)),   streamline_data = list(mean_FA = 0.475) )  set.seed(42) bun <- bundle(lapply(seq_len(6), function(i) {   noise <- matrix(rnorm(nrow(pts) * 3, sd = 0.2), ncol = 3)   colnames(noise) <- c("X", "Y", "Z")   streamline(     points          = pts + noise,     point_data      = list(FA = pmin(pmax(sl@point_data$FA + rnorm(6, sd = 0.05), 0), 1)),     streamline_data = list(mean_FA = mean(sl@point_data$FA))   ) }))

what: fatten() method for fiber::bundle objects — fatten-fiber-bundle-method
title: fatten() method for fiber::bundle objects — fatten-fiber-bundle-method
text: Assigns visible tube radius every fiber::streamline fiber::bundle. streamlines sparse whole bundle kept radius half minimal inter-streamline separation; dense bundle pruned non-overlapping, hull-covering subset visibility floor. See fatten() full parameter documentation.

title: fatten() method for fiber::bundle objects — fatten-fiber-bundle-method
text: x fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, fiber::bundle_set. visibility Numeric. smallest tube radius considered visible naked eye. NULL (default) derives streamlines' sampling density (median intra-streamline step); positive number overrides floor. ... Reserved future arguments.

title: fatten() method for fiber::bundle objects — fatten-fiber-bundle-method
text: fiber::bundle every streamline carries per-streamline radius; dense bundles hold pruned subset streamlines.

title: fatten() method for fiber::bundle objects — fatten-fiber-bundle-method
code:
library(fiber)  # Six line-only streamlines: six helix strands fanning apart in the lateral # (Y) direction, each sampled at a 0.1 mm step. They are far enough apart # that a visible tube radius keeps them from colliding: the sparse regime. strand <- function(i) {   t <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 200)   fiber::streamline(cbind(     X = seq_len(200) * 0.1,     Y = 0.25 * sin(t + 1.3 * i) + (i - 3.5) * 1.2,     Z = 0.25 * cos(t) + (i - 3.5) * 0.15   )) } bun <- fiber::bundle(lapply(seq_len(6), strand))  # Every streamline now carries a per-streamline radius, and all six survive. fattened <- fatten(bun) length(fattened@streamlines) #> [1] 6 plot3d(fattened)              # draws real 3D tubes #> ℹ Rendering 6 streamlines...  {"x":{"mode":"tube","positions":"zczMPUSVMMAAAAC+zcxMPv1XMMCfggC+mpmZPrAqMMD5CQK+zczMPowNMMB8lAS+AAAAP64A

title: fatten() method for fiber::bundle_set objects — fatten-fiber-bundle_set-method
text: Fatens every fiber::bundle fiber::bundle_set independently, visibility floor pruning decision, returns set resulting bundles. See fatten() full parameter documentation.

title: fatten() method for fiber::bundle_set objects — fatten-fiber-bundle_set-method
text: x fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, fiber::bundle_set. visibility Numeric. smallest tube radius considered visible naked eye. NULL (default) derives streamlines' sampling density (median intra-streamline step); positive number overrides floor. ... Reserved future arguments.

title: fatten() method for fiber::bundle_set objects — fatten-fiber-bundle_set-method
text: fiber::bundle_set every streamline carries per-streamline radius; dense bundles hold pruned subset, bundles pruned zero streamlines dropped.

library(fiber)  # Two bundles of line-only streamlines in one set: a sparse fanning tract and # a densely packed one. Each is fattened independently. fan <- function(i) {   t <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 200)   fiber::streamline(cbind(     X = seq_len(200) * 0.1,     Y = 0.25 * sin(t) + (i - 3.5) * 1.5,     Z = 0.25 * cos(t)   )) } pack <- function(i) {   t <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 100)   fiber::streamline(cbind(     X = seq_len(100) * 0.5,     Y = 0.5 + (i - 3.5) * 0.3,     Z = 0.25 * sin(t) + (i - 3.5) * 0.05   )) } cs <- fiber::bundle_set(list(   fan  = fiber::bundle(lapply(seq_len(6), fan)),   pack = fiber::bundle(lapply(seq_len(6), pack)) ))  fattened <- fatten(cs) vapply(fattened@bundles, function(b) length(b@streamlines), integer(1L)) #> [1] 6 2 plot3d(fattened)              # draws real 3D tubes per bundle #> ℹ Rendering 8 streamlines across 2 bundles...  {"x":{"mode":"tube","positions":"zczMPQAAcMAAAIA+zcxMPoX9bsBhfX8+mpmZPhL8bcAH9n0+zczMPq38bMCEa3s+AAAAP1sA

text: x fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, fiber::bundle_set. visibility Numeric. smallest tube radius considered visible naked eye. NULL (default) derives streamlines' sampling density (median intra-streamline step); positive number overrides floor. ... Reserved future arguments.

title: Assign a visible tube radius to line-only streamlines — fatten
text: fatten() gives fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, fiber::bundle_set carries radius data tube radius guaranteed visible naked eye, stores back object per-streamline radius key. plot3d() reports radius data object already carries, prune() thins bundle non-overlapping subset radius choose, prune() gives full control tunable engine. fatten() convenience wrapper picks radius reuses prune()'s selection logic internally dense case: afterwards plain plot3d() call draws real 3D tubes. rather pick radius clearance tubes , call prune() directly instead. radius chosen geometry streamlines : Sparse streamlines (far apart relative visibility floor) keep fibres get constant radius equal half minimal distance two streamlines, adjacent tubes just touch nothing hidden. Dense streamlines (packed closer floor) pruned non-overlapping, hull-covering subset floor radius, preserving many streamlines can shown without overlap visible size. visibility floor median distance consecutive sampled points streamlines (sampling density); tube treated visible radius reaches spacing. Override visibility.

title: Assign a visible tube radius to line-only streamlines — fatten

title: Assign a visible tube radius to line-only streamlines — fatten
text: x fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, fiber::bundle_set. visibility Numeric. smallest tube radius considered visible naked eye. NULL (default) derives streamlines' sampling density (median intra-streamline step); positive number overrides floor. ... Reserved future arguments.

title: plot3d() method for fiber::bundle objects — plot3d-fiber-bundle-method
text: x fiber::bundle object. color Controls streamline colours assigned. Accepted values: "orientation" (default): per-point RGB colour derived local fibre direction. absolute values normalised tangent vector \((|dx|, |dy|, |dz|)\) mapped R, G, B channels — standard DTI colour convention (left-right = red, anterior-posterior = green, superior-inferior = blue). metadata key: string matching key @point_data (per-point scalar) @streamline_data (per-streamline scalar, broadcast points). Numeric values mapped continuous colour scale (palette); character values coloured categorically. CSS/hex colour string: e.g. "#E69F00" "steelblue". lines drawn fixed colour. palette plotly / ColorBrewer colour scale name applied color numeric metadata key. Defaults "Viridis". backend Character. htmlwidget renderer use: "threejs" (default) "plotly". three.js backend supports real world-space line thickness (true 3D tubes) object-level depth-sorted transparency; plotly backend opt-alternative interactive plotly-style charts. linewidth Numeric. title: plot3d() method for fiber::bundle_set objects — plot3d-fiber-bundle_set-method
text: x fiber::bundle_set object. color Controls streamline colours assigned. Accepted values: "orientation" (default): per-point RGB colour derived local fibre direction. absolute values normalised tangent vector \((|dx|, |dy|, |dz|)\) mapped R, G, B channels — standard DTI colour convention (left-right = red, anterior-posterior = green, superior-inferior = blue). metadata key: string matching key @point_data (per-point scalar) @streamline_data (per-streamline scalar, broadcast points). Numeric values mapped continuous colour scale (palette); character values coloured categorically. CSS/hex colour string: e.g. "#E69F00" "steelblue". lines drawn fixed colour. palette plotly / ColorBrewer colour scale name applied color numeric metadata key. Defaults "Viridis". backend Character. htmlwidget renderer use: "threejs" (default) "plotly". three.js backend supports real world-space line thickness (true 3D tubes) object-level depth-sorted transparency; plotly backend opt-alternative interactive plotly-style charts. linewidth Numeric. Width plotted lines. Defaults 2. three.js backend maps THREE.LineBasicMaterial.linewidth, WebGL caps 1 platforms; use radius genuinely thick fibres. radius Numeric radius world units (three.js backend ). knob true 3D tubes; separate thickness argument. radius treated data carried object: radius NULL (default), radius key streamlines' @point_data (per-point) @streamline_data (per-streamline) picked rendered real 3D tubes; tubes drawn exactly radius, never shrunk avoid overlap neighbouring fibres (overlap generator's business, rtists's). explicit radius argument overrides data. Accepts: NULL (default): draw object's radius data present, otherwise thin lines (fast Line2 linewidth). scalar 0: fast flat Line2 linewidth (nothing needs tube). positive scalar: every streamline drawn real 3D TubeGeometry tube constant world radius, genuine thickness, Phong flat shading, object-level depth-sorted transparency (tube mesh sorted back--front). per-streamline vector (length == number streamlines): one constant radius per line, drawn TubeGeometry. per-point vector (length == total number points): radius varying along streamline, drawn TubeGeometry radial displacement — general form. opacity Numeric [0, 1]. Global line opacity. Defaults 0.5. bg Background colour (CSS) scene (three.js backend ). Defaults "#111111". color_by_bundle Logical. TRUE, every streamline coloured parent bundle name (one distinct colour per entry set), overriding color argument. FALSE (default), color applied -, inheriting per-streamline colouring behaviour fiber::bundle method. tooltip Hover tooltip three.js backend. point streamline hovered, -scene tooltip shows bundle's name, point's 3D coordinates, values attributes. Accepted values: TRUE (default): show bundle name (object carries one), coordinates, attributes recorded object (per-point, per-streamline, per-bundle per-bundle-set alike). FALSE: disable tooltip entirely. character vector attribute column names: show , alongside always-included coordinates (bundle name present). Names exist object ignored. Right-clicking hovered tooltip opens checkbox list every toggleable column; ticking unticking one updates visible box immediately. bundle name coordinates stay pinned toggled . plotly backend ignores argument (plotly surface carries hover). ... Additional named arguments. plotly backend uses , forwarding plotly::layout() (e.g. title = "bundle"); three.js backend (default) ignores .

library(fiber)  # Three white-matter tracts that all run through the centrum semiovale: # the pyramidal/corticospinal tract (CST, vertical/fanning), the superior # longitudinal fasciculus (SLF, anterior-posterior) and the corpus callosum # (CC, left-right). Drawn to pass through the origin they cross there, # producing the classic DTI orientation colours: CST blue (superior- # inferior), SLF green (anterior-posterior), CC red (left-right). cst_sl <- function(i) {   t   <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 120)      # -1 deep, +1 cortex   fan <- (t + 1) / 2   streamline(cbind(     X = 0.5 * sin(0.7 * t) + (i - 3.5) * 0.22 * (0.30 + 0.85 * fan),     Y = 0.4 * cos(0.5 * t) + (i - 3.5) * 0.10 * (0.30 + 0.85 * fan),     Z = 4 * t   )) } cc_sl <- function(i) {   t <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 120)   streamline(cbind(     X = 6 * t,     Y = 0.35 * t * t + (i - 3.5) * 0.18 * (1 + 0.4 * abs(t)),     Z = 0.3 * sin(pi * t) + (i - 3.5) * 0.12   )) } slf_sl <- function(i) {   t <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 120)   streamline(cbind(     X = 0.35 * sin(pi * t) + (i - 3.5) * 0.15,     Y = 6 * t,     Z = 0.5 * sin(0.8 * t) + (i - 3.5) * 0.14   )) } cst <- bundle(lapply(seq_len(8), cst_sl)) cc  <- bundle(lapply(seq_len(8), cc_sl)) slf <- bundle(lapply(seq_len(8), slf_sl)) cs  <- bundle_set(list(CST = cst, CC = cc, SLF = slf))  # Orientation-coloured crossing bundles (the triple-colour crossing). plot3d(cs) #> ℹ Rendering 24 streamlines across 3 bundles...  {"x":{"mode":"line2","positions":"VWb5vjNUjT4AAIDApRj5vr47jT6OsnvApRj5vr47jT6OsnvAM8X4vgQgjT4cZXfAM8X4vgQg

what: plot3d() method for fiber::streamline objects — plot3d-fiber-streamline-method
title: plot3d() method for fiber::streamline objects — plot3d-fiber-streamline-method
text: Renders single fiber::streamline interactive 3D line plot. See plot3d() full parameter documentation examples.

title: plot3d() method for fiber::streamline objects — plot3d-fiber-streamline-method
text: x fiber::streamline object. color Controls streamline colours assigned. Accepted values: "orientation" (default): per-point RGB colour derived local fibre direction. absolute values normalised tangent vector \((|dx|, |dy|, |dz|)\) mapped R, G, B channels — standard DTI colour convention (left-right = red, anterior-posterior = green, superior-inferior = blue). metadata key: string matching key @point_data (per-point scalar) @streamline_data (per-streamline scalar, broadcast points). Numeric values mapped continuous colour scale (palette); character values coloured categorically. CSS/hex colour string: e.g. "#E69F00" "steelblue". lines drawn fixed colour. palette plotly / ColorBrewer colour scale name applied color numeric metadata key. Defaults "Viridis". backend Character. htmlwidget renderer use: "threejs" (default) "plotly". three.js backend supports real world-space line thickness (true 3D tubes) object-level depth-sorted transparency; plotly backend opt-alternative interactive plotly-style charts. linewidth Numeric. Width plotted lines. Defaults 2. three.js backend maps THREE.LineBasicMaterial.linewidth, WebGL caps 1 platforms; use radius genuinely thick fibres. radius Numeric radius world units (three.js backend ). knob true 3D tubes; separate thickness argument. radius treated data carried object: radius NULL (default), radius key streamlines' @point_data (per-point) @streamline_data (per-streamline) picked rendered real 3D tubes; tubes drawn exactly radius, never shrunk avoid overlap neighbouring fibres (overlap generator's business, rtists's). explicit radius argument overrides data. Accepts: NULL (default): draw object's radius data present, otherwise thin lines (fast Line2 linewidth). scalar 0: fast flat Line2 linewidth (nothing needs tube). positive scalar: every streamline drawn real 3D TubeGeometry tube constant world radius, genuine thickness, Phong flat shading, object-level depth-sorted transparency (tube mesh sorted back--front). per-streamline vector (length == number streamlines): one constant radius per line, drawn TubeGeometry. per-point vector (length == total number points): radius varying along streamline, drawn TubeGeometry radial displacement — general form. opacity Numeric [0, 1]. Global line opacity. Defaults 0.5. bg Background colour (CSS) scene (three.js backend ). Defaults "#111111". tooltip Hover tooltip three.js backend. point streamline hovered, -scene tooltip shows bundle's name, point's 3D coordinates, values attributes. Accepted values: TRUE (default): show bundle name (object carries one), coordinates, attributes recorded object (per-point, per-streamline, per-bundle per-bundle-set alike). FALSE: disable tooltip entirely. character vector attribute column names: show , alongside always-included coordinates (bundle name present). Names exist object ignored. what: Interactive 3D line plot for tractography streamlines and bundles — plot3d
title: Interactive 3D line plot for tractography streamlines and bundles — plot3d
text: plot3d() S7 generic produces interactive 3D plot tractography objects fiber package. Two htmlwidget backends available: "threejs" (default): self-contained three.js renderer real world-space line thickness (true 3D tubes), depth-sorted transparency, fast single-mesh line mode scales large bundles. "plotly": scatter3d line plot streamlines share one trace separated NA break-points. deliberately opt-alternative renderer prefer interactive plotly surface. Methods available following classes: fiber::bundle fiber::bundle_set fiber::streamline

title: Interactive 3D line plot for tractography streamlines and bundles — plot3d
code: plot3d(   x,   color = "orientation",   palette = "Viridis",   backend = c("threejs", "plotly"),   linewidth = 2,   radius = NULL,   opacity = 0.5,   bg = "#111111",   tooltip = TRUE,   ... )

title: Interactive 3D line plot for tractography streamlines and bundles — plot3d
text: x fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, fiber::bundle_set object. color Controls streamline colours assigned. Accepted values: "orientation" (default): per-point RGB colour derived local fibre direction. absolute values normalised tangent vector \((|dx|, |dy|, |dz|)\) mapped R, G, B channels — standard DTI colour convention (left-right = red, anterior-posterior = green, superior-inferior = blue). metadata key: string matching key @point_data (per-point scalar) @streamline_data (per-streamline scalar, broadcast points). Numeric values mapped continuous colour scale (palette); character values coloured categorically. CSS/hex colour string: e.g. "#E69F00" "steelblue". lines drawn fixed colour. palette plotly / ColorBrewer colour scale name applied color numeric metadata key. Defaults "Viridis". backend Character. htmlwidget renderer use: "threejs" (default) "plotly". three.js backend supports real world-space line thickness (true 3D tubes) object-level depth-sorted transparency; plotly backend opt-alternative interactive plotly-style charts. linewidth Numeric. Width plotted lines. Defaults 2. three.js backend maps THREE.LineBasicMaterial.linewidth, WebGL caps 1 platforms; use radius genuinely thick fibres. radius Numeric radius world units (three.js backend ). knob true 3D tubes; separate thickness argument. radius treated data carried object: radius NULL (default), radius key streamlines' @point_data (per-point) @streamline_data (per-streamline) picked rendered real 3D tubes; tubes drawn exactly radius, never shrunk avoid overlap neighbouring fibres (overlap generator's business, rtists's). explicit radius argument overrides data. Accepts: NULL (default): draw object's radius data present, otherwise thin lines (fast Line2 linewidth). scalar 0: fast flat Line2 linewidth (nothing needs tube). positive scalar: every streamline drawn real 3D TubeGeometry tube constant world radius, genuine thickness, Phong flat shading, object-level depth-sorted transparency (tube mesh sorted back--front). per-streamline vector (length == number streamlines): one constant radius per line, drawn TubeGeometry. per-point vector (length == total number points): radius varying along streamline, drawn TubeGeometry radial displacement — general form. opacity Numeric [0, 1]. Global line opacity. Defaults 0.5. bg Background colour (CSS) scene (three.js backend ). Defaults "#111111". tooltip Hover tooltip three.js backend. point streamline hovered, -scene tooltip shows bundle's name, point's 3D coordinates, values attributes. Accepted values: TRUE (default): show bundle name (object carries one), coordinates, attributes recorded object (per-point, per-streamline, per-bundle per-bundle-set alike). FALSE: disable tooltip entirely. character vector attribute column names: show , alongside always-included coordinates (bundle name present). Names exist object ignored. Right-clicking hovered tooltip opens checkbox list every toggleable column; ticking unticking one updates visible box immediately. bundle name coordinates stay pinned toggled . plotly backend ignores argument (plotly surface carries hover). ... Additional named arguments. plotly backend uses , forwarding plotly::layout() (e.g. title = "bundle"); three.js backend (default) ignores .

title: prune() method for fiber::bundle objects — prune-fiber-bundle-method
code: library(fiber)  # Six line-only streamlines in a bundle (no radius data on them). Rendered # as thin lines by default; if you want to draw them as fat tubes you would # pick a radius yourself. At radius 1 the six packed strands overlap. sl  <- streamline(cbind(X = seq_len(200) * 0.1,                         Y = 0.25 * sin(seq_len(200) / 200 * 4 * pi),                         Z = 0.25 * cos(seq_len(200) / 200 * 4 * pi))) strand <- function(i) {   t <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 200)   streamline(cbind(     X = seq_len(200) * 0.1,     Y = 0.25 * sin(t + 1.3 * i) + (i - 3.5) * 1.2,     Z = 0.25 * cos(t) + (i - 3.5) * 0.15   )) } bun <- bundle(lapply(seq_len(6), strand))  # Because the tubes are fabricated by you from line-only data, prune keeps # a spread-out subset whose fat tubes do not overlap: the extreme strands. pruned <- prune(bun, radius = 1) length(pruned@streamlines) #> [1] 2

title: rtists 0.1.0
text: Initial CRAN release. Added plot3d(), S7 generic methods fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, fiber::bundle_set objects. "threejs": self-contained three.js renderer (CDN). thickness > 0 draws real world-space tubes per-point colour object-level depth-sorted transparency; fast line mode scales large bundles. "plotly": single scatter3d trace separated NA break-points, retained interim fallback. "orientation" (default): per-point RGB colour derived local fibre direction using standard DTI convention (left–right = red, anterior–posterior = green, superior–inferior = blue). Metadata key: key @point_data @streamline_data can mapped continuous (palette) categorical colour scale. Fixed colour: CSS colour name hex string. Interactive figures support pan, rotate, zoom.

title: rtists 0.1.0
text: static (non-Shiny) htmlwidgets path fixed: three.js backend, ESM renderer module imported asynchronously, can register widget binding htmlwidgets’ initial staticRender() (run DOMContentLoaded). console Viewer pane therefore produced canvas error. loader now re-invokes Shiny’s binding scan HTMLWidgets.staticRender() module ready. re-render idempotent, widgets left untouched. Named bundles honoured correctly plot3d(): per-bundle input names recorded fiber::bundle_set() now read right slot (@bundle_data), bundle_set built named list keeps names instead falling back sequential indices.
